A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InvAD research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original anomaly-detection results on industrial and medical benchmarks, together with ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds inversion-schedule and feature-resolution ablations in supplementary Tables 13-14.

M1.justification: The feature-space diffusion model, DDIM inversion, and scoring procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 removes the redundant absolute value around max(A)-min(A), which is already nonnegative. Specifying bilinear interpolation adds implementation detail without establishing a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MVTecAD, VisA, MPDD, and the same BMAD medical datasets. The new ablations vary model settings and stratify existing MVTecAD cases by anomaly size; they introduce no additional dataset, domain, or task.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the benchmark and generalizability experiments remains unchanged. The added attribution for the existing no-inversion ablation does not introduce a new comparison row; the new schedule and resolution variants are ablation settings.

E3.justification: New protocols compare four inversion schedules at S=3, 10, and 100, and feature resolutions of 8x8, 16x16, and 24x24 using anomaly-size-stratified mAD. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged; warmup and cosine decay are still documented in Table 11 despite shortening the main-text description.

E4.justification: Supplementary Section 9 adds targeted sensitivity analyses of inversion scheduling and feature resolution, including small-anomaly performance. These extend the existing step-count, component, backbone, scoring, and qualitative analyses, which are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same statement about fixing library seeds and disabling nondeterministic GPU operations where possible. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the new tables add no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are retained. Tables 13-14 add results: uniform scheduling at S=3 yields 83.35 mAD versus 81.48-82.37 for alternatives, while overall mAD for 8x8, 16x16, and 24x24 features is 82.05, 83.70, and 81.44. These are additional ablation findings, not improved main benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations and DDIM-inversion derivation are retained, including supplementary Equations 9-21. The scoring simplification is mathematically equivalent, and the added scheduling formulas specify experimental controls rather than new theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the reconstruction-free inversion contribution, strong detection-performance claims, approximately twofold inference speedup, and applicability to existing diffusion models. The additional experiments support retained claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v4 adds discussion of feature compression potentially obscuring small anomalies and interprets the resolution ablation as showing that higher resolution is not monotonically beneficial. It also explains the uniform-schedule choice and expands the fairness rationale for EfficientNet. Existing reverse-scoring explanations and limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 specifies bilinear anomaly-map interpolation, and Section 4.7 clarifies the existing no-inversion ablation's skipped algorithm steps and scoring attribution. v4 adds a project-page link while retaining the original code link in the supplement. Hardware, hyperparameters, and training-time disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds Li et al.'s prototype-oriented diffusion work and Rippel et al.'s pretrained-feature anomaly-detection work, supporting limited positioning and attribution additions. Most other reference changes concern formatting or bibliographic metadata rather than different cited research.

P1.justification: v4 makes local wording and spelling corrections, renames Abs to Diff, updates author/contact notes, and standardizes references. Funding acknowledgment becomes a separate section, and the supplement gains an ablation section; the main narrative structure remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 13-14 and reflows the supplement, relocating the unchanged Figure 4 plots. It also corrects the RESC detection-column heading in Table 3 and updates scoring labels in Table 9 and Figure 4. Existing visual designs are largely retained.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3, the added sensitivity studies provide useful evidence for existing schedule and resolution choices, while implementation clarifications and labeling corrections improve clarity. The gain is limited by unspecified anomaly-size cutoffs and the unexplained nominal-default mAD discrepancy between Table 13 (83.35) and Table 2 (83.7). The core method and primary evidence remain unchanged.
